newsitem.title: UK: U.K. North Sea November oil output hits 1996 high.
newsitem.headline: U.K. North Sea November oil output hits 1996 high.

text.p: U.K. North Sea oil output rose by 69,280 barrels per day (bpd) in November to reach 2,678,227 bpd, setting a new record for 1996, the Aberdeen Petroleum report said on Friday.
The November figure was the highest level since November 1995, it said.
The November total included contributions from new fields achieving their first full month's production.
Of these, Shell Expro's Teal/Teal South/Guillemot complex yielded 41,000 bpd, Ranger's Columba B contributed 8,402 bpd and Amerada Hess' Telford, a satellite of the Scott field, 7,026 bpd.
A Shell Expro official said last month the Teal area would reach peak production of 60,000 bpd by the end of the year. Shell Expro is a 50/50 joint venture between Royal Dutch/Shell and Exxon Corp.
Enterprise's Nelson field, whose production declined by 16,151 bpd in November, was the mature field to show the biggest monthly fall.

"Compensation came from Agip's Tiffany/Toni/Thelma group of fields with a 33,268 bpd increase, reflecting a return to full production in the wake of the Thelma start-up," the report added. -- London newsroom +44 1717 542 4088
